BUDGET OVERSIGHT COMMITTEE MINUTES
  TUESDAY, SEPTEMBER 8, 2026
  411 W. OCEAN BOULEVARD
  CIVIC CHAMBERS, 1:00 PM

Dr. Joni Ricks-Oddie, Chair
Roberto Uranga, Vice Chair
Cindy Allen, Member

  FINISHED AGENDA & DRAFT MINUTES

 Note: Due to a technical issue, the recording of the meeting is missing the first 35 minutes and starts
  when the meeting resumed from a recess during Agenda Item No. 3.

CALL TO ORDER

At 1:01 PM, Chair Ricks-Oddie called the meeting to order.

ROLL CALL

Councilmembers Present: Allen, Uranga, Ricks-Oddie

Also present: Rebecca Bernstorff, Budget Manager, Financial Management, Ashleigh Stone, Deputy
City Attorney, Jonathan Nagayama, City Clerk Analyst.

REGULAR AGENDA

1.  26-55978  Recommendation to approve the minutes for the Budget Oversight Committee
  meeting of Tuesday, September 1, 2026.

  A motion was made by Member Allen, seconded by Chair Ricks-Oddie, to
  approve recommendation. The motion carried by the following vote:

  Yes:  3  Allen, Uranga, Ricks-Oddie
  No:  0  None
  Recused: 0  None
  Absent: 0  None

2.  26-55979  Recommendation to receive and file a list of follow-up items from the Budget
  Hearings and/or Budget Oversight Committee meetings.

  A motion was made by Vice Chair Uranga, seconded by Member Allen, to
  approve recommendation. The motion carried by the following vote:

  Yes:  3 Allen, Uranga, Ricks-Oddie
  No:  0 None

  Rebecca Bernstorff, Budget Manager, Financial Management, spoke.

  Chair Ricks-Oddie spoke.

3.  26-55980  Recommendation to forward the Budget Oversight Committee’s FY 27 Budget
  recommendations for Council consideration.

  A motion was made by Vice Chair Uranga, seconded by Member Allen, to
  approve recommendation, as amended, to:

  [B] Motion to support the Budget Oversight Committee’s Proposed Budget
  Recommendations and changes to the Mayor’s Budget Recommendations
  and appropriate the following one-time and structural enhancements or
  provide policy direction:

  [B1] Motion repealing the previous one percent (1%) tax rate reduction for
  cannabis adult-use retailers, increasing the tax rate from seven percent (7%)
  to eight percent (8%), which is below the maximum of twelve percent (12%);
  and also, setting the rate for cannabis cultivators at $15.00 per square foot
  under cultivation. The adjustment to the tax rate for cannabis cultivators is
  equivalent to 1) repealing the one percent (1%) equivalent reduction in the tax
  rate from $14.96 to $13.09 per square foot under cultivation passed by the
  City Council in 2024; 2) allowing the annual Consumer Price Index (CPI)
  adjustment to the new tax rate to take effect on October 1, 2026. These
  adjustments would result in a tax rate well over $15.00 per square foot under
  cultivation. This action is estimated to bring back General Fund Group
  revenues in the amount of $1,154,304 to further support its intended use of
  regulation and enforcement, and Public Health and Safety services.

  [B2] Motion to recognize revenue estimated to be $1,500,000 in the General
  Fund Group, from the increase in specific parking citations to $100, as
  outlined in the FY 27 proposed fee schedule, to offset structural costs
  proposed by the Budget Oversight Committee. These include fines such as
  parking in bike lanes, red curbs, fire hydrants, and no parking zones.

  [B3] Motion to amend the FY 27 proposed Master Fee and Charges Schedule
  to raise street sweeping parking citations rates from $75 to $80 and recognize
  revenue estimated to be $700,000 in the General Fund Group, to offset
  structural costs proposed by the Budget Oversight Committee.

  [B4] Motion to restore $1,275,575 and 11 FTEs in the General Fund Group in
  the Library, Arts & Culture Department, offset by $150,623 by reallocating

  Page 2 of 11
   BUDGET OVERSIGHT COMMITTEE MINUTES
  TUESDAY, SEPTEMBER 8, 2026
  411 W. OCEAN BOULEVARD
  CIVIC CHAMBERS, 1:00 PM

funding from the Mayor's Recommendations plan to support SB 707 costs,
contingent on the revised Council meeting plan to be approved by October 1,
and $1,124,952 in revenue generated by increased parking citations, to
preserve Monday hours at the Bay Shore, Burnett, El Dorado, Harte, and
Michelle Obama Neighborhood Libraries. This includes the restoration of 5
Library Clerks, 4 Library Assistants, a vacant General Librarian in Education
and Outreach Services at Billie Jean King (BJK) Main Library, 1.0 FTE of Page
hours, the overtime budget for Monday hours, and a restored budget for
Security Services.

[B5] Motion to restore $932,000 in the General Fund Group in the Police
Department, offset by $610,000 from the proposed action on cannabis tax
revenue, and $322,000 in proposed revenue generated by increasing street
sweeping parking citations, 1 FTE Quality of Life Police Sergeant and 2 FTE
Quality of Life Police Officers from the City Manager’s proposal to eliminate a
Quality of Life Police Sergeant and six Quality of Life Police Officers in the
Collaborative Response Division. With the Mayor's Recommendations, this
action brings the total restored positions to 4 Quality of Life Police Officers
and 1 Quality of Life Police Sergeant FTEs, and the total critical services
section to 6 Quality of Life Police Officers and 2 Quality of Life Police
Sergeants.

[B6] Motion to add structural funds of $131,969 in the General Fund Group in
the Fire Department, offset by revenue generated by increased parking
citations, to convert Engine 22 to a Paramedic Assessment Unit, so that all
three responding engines surrounding Station 14 are now paramedic
assessment units.

[B7] Motion to add one-time funds of $103,120 in the General Fund Group in
the Citywide Activities Department, offset by the Mayor's Recommendations
one-time dollars for utilization by the Budget Oversight Committee and City
Council to further community priorities and budget restorations on a one-time
basis, to support priority initiatives identified by each Council District that
improve neighborhood and community services, divided equally between the
City Council Districts for District Priorities.

[B8] Motion to add structural funds of $50,000 in the General Fund Group in
the City Manager Department, offset by revenue generated by increased
parking citations, to fund Summer Block Parties and Neighborhood
Activations.

[B9] Motion to add one-time funds of $200,000 in the General Fund Group in
the Fire Department, offset by the Mayor's Recommendations one-time
dollars for utilization by the Budget Oversight Committee and City Council to
further community priorities and budget restorations on a one-time basis, to

  Page 3 of 11
   BUDGET OVERSIGHT COMMITTEE MINUTES
  TUESDAY, SEPTEMBER 8, 2026

  CIVIC CHAMBERS, 1:00 PM

fund an independent, third-party Long Beach Fire and Emergency Medical
Services Financial Sustainability and Governance Feasibility Study, building
upon the City’s previously completed Fire Optimization and Emergency
Medical Services analyses.

[B10] Motion to add $325,000 in the General Fund Group in the Health and
Human Services Department, offset by $33,921 from the action on cannabis
tax revenue, $98,000 from proposed revenue generated by increasing street
sweeping parking citations, and $193,079 from revenue generated by
increased parking citations, to structurally fund the Safe Passage Program.

[B11] Motion to add $272,234 in the General Fund Group in the Health and
Human Services Department, offset by the action on cannabis tax revenue, to
structurally fund the Complaint Response Unit, a coordinated effort to
enforce regulations against unpermitted sidewalk food vendors, to help
educate vendors, discard food, and confiscate unpermitted food vending
equipment.

[B12] Motion to recognize the extension of the City’s tree trimming cycle from
six years to eight years and the associated reduction of $522,000 in
unbudgeted costs that would otherwise be required to maintain the current
six-year cycle; support the existing proposal for a position in the Public
Works Department to support an equity-based pilot program providing
sliding-scale rebates to residents who wish to participate in more frequent
tree trimming; add structural funds of $50,000 in the General Fund Group in
the Public Works Department, offset by proposed revenue generated by
increasing street sweeping parking citations, to provide seed funding for
rebates through the pilot program; and request that the City Manager,
through the Public Works Department, report back to the City Council after 6
months of the pilot’s start, on the pilot program’s implementation,
participation, outcomes, and recommendations for future funding.

[B13] Motion to partially restore $230,000 in the General Fund Group in the
Parks, Recreation & Marine Department, offset by proposed revenue
generated by increasing street sweeping parking citations with $115,000 to
support weed abatement services and $115,000 to partially restore reductions
to Materials, Supplies, and Services to support planting projects,
maintenance of vandalized items, replacement of damaged safety cones,
signs, barricades, and other deferred maintenance and operational needs.

[B14] Motion to add structural funds of $238,149 in the General Fund Group in
the City Manager Department, offset by the action on cannabis tax revenue, to
bring on a Program Specialist along with operational support needs (if
funding remains after accounting for the full cost of the position) to establish
and lead a dedicated human trafficking and sexual exploitation focus area

  Page 4 of 11
   BUDGET OVERSIGHT COMMITTEE MINUTES
  TUESDAY, SEPTEMBER 8, 2026
  411 W. OCEAN BOULEVARD
  CIVIC CHAMBERS, 1:00 PM

and serve as the City’s centralized lead for implementation and coordination
of the R.E.A.C.T. Framework and related interdepartmental and
interjurisdictional efforts, consistent with the City’s adopted legislative
priorities, which identify combating human trafficking as a top legislative
priority, as recommended by the Intergovernmental Affairs Committee and
approved by the City Council.

[B15] Motion to direct $200,000 in funding within County Measure A
LACAHSA to support a Community Land Trust (CLT) a non-profit, mission-
driven organization with a demonstrated commitment to affordable housing
preservation, community stewardship, and equitable ownership models. The
funding is intended to leverage additional financing for the acquisition and
long-term sustainability of lower income housing under a CLT. This shall be a
competitive funding opportunity and the application criteria shall include how
the grant will lead to sustainable operations without further city funding.

[B16] Motion to reduce the Mayor's Recommendation (Motion A10) of
restoring $86,150 for half a Public Health Professional III in the Office of
Veteran Affairs (OVA) to $61,150 towards funding a position and reallocate
$25,000 towards the Veterans Banner Program ($20,000 for banners and
$5,000 for recognition service of those on the banners) in the General Fund
Group in the Health and Human Services Department.

[B17] Motion to direct the City Manager to establish a three-year partnership
with the Long Beach Public Library Foundation and its $250,000 annual
funding commitment to support the Creativity Lab and its modified
programming and services, leveraging philanthropic partnership to preserve
this important community resource and augment efforts currently funded with
Measure US funds, with the understanding that the City’s financial
commitment will not increase to offset any shortfall in the Foundation’s
annual funding commitment and that programming and services will be
adjusted or discontinued, as necessary, based on available funding.

[B18] Motion to recognize the City Manager's proposed $140,000 in one-time
funding in the Special Advertising and Promotion Fund Group for the
Juneteenth Celebration and clarify that the funding is intended as seed
funding for the City to establish and host a City-led Juneteenth Celebration
for the community.

[B19] Motion to recognize the City Manager's proposed $50,000 in one-time
funding for the Long Beach Walls and Community Art Murals program and
direct the City Manager to encourage geographic dispersion of funded
projects throughout the City when considering investments, with
consideration given to providing opportunities for neighborhoods across
Long Beach to participate.

  Page 5 of 11
   BUDGET OVERSIGHT COMMITTEE MINUTES
  TUESDAY, SEPTEMBER 8, 2026
  411 W. OCEAN BOULEVARD
  CIVIC CHAMBERS, 1:00 PM

[B20] Motion to add one-time funding of $120,000 in the General Fund Group
in the City Manager Department to fund an Electric Vehicle Battery Reuse and
Recycling Hub Feasibility Study, consistent with the recommendation of the
Climate Resilient and Sustainable City Commission, and $30,000 in one-time
funding in the General Fund Group in the Public Works Department to
support initial planning, regulatory engagement, and stakeholder
coordination related to exploring an umbrella mitigation bank in Long Beach,
recognizing that both efforts support the planning and development of
potential City infrastructure and are eligible uses of City Measure A funds,
offset by reserving $150,000 from FY 26 City Measure A critical needs funds
to be set asides and carried over to FY 27. Additionally, reallocate $150,000
for the Marine Amphitheatre Feasibility Study within the City Measure A
Elevate 28’ FY 27 bond program to the Critical Infrastructure Reserve.

[B21] Motion to direct the City Manager to work with the Public Works
Department to amend the adopted Fiscal Year 2024 Budget action to adjust
the City Place Parking Garage rates from one hour free with $2.00 per hour
with a $12 daily maximum to 90 minutes free and $2.00 per 30 minutes with a
$12 daily maximum. This amended action is expected to generate an
additional $250,000 in General Fund revenue at the City Place Parking Garage
which will be reinvested into the City Place Parking Garage assets and the
surrounding area. Additionally, this funding will structurally fund the publicly
accessible secured restroom located at Harvey Milk Park for parking patrons,
as well as the general public.

[B22] Motion to direct the City Manager to work with the Police Department to
request that the County of Los Angeles provide a financial support match to
the $394,701 in the Mayor's Recommendations to provide clean up support
along Los Angeles County Rivers.

[B23] Motion to request the City Manager and Utilities Department work
together to review all approved AB 32 projects and allocations to determine
whether any funds may be available to repurpose to support citywide
priorities, aimed at reducing operational costs and GHG emissions, and
improving infrastructure; determine feasibility of City Council project
priorities such as the Solar Streetlight Conversion Program to enhance the
City's streetlights and conversion to solar which will reduce the threat of
vandalism and inoperability while reducing GHG emissions through removing
reliance on hard-wired power; and present any updates on project
reallocations to the Utilities Board and update the City Council via
memorandum.

[B24] Motion to request the City Manager to expressly allow up to $500,000 in
settlement assistance funding as an allowable use under the County Measure

  Page 6 of 11
   BUDGET OVERSIGHT COMMITTEE MINUTES
  TUESDAY, SEPTEMBER 8, 2026
  411 W. OCEAN BOULEVARD
  CIVIC CHAMBERS, 1:00 PM

A category of Homeless Prevention and Rental Assistance.

[B25] Motion to request that the City Manager establish a limit of no more
than two regular meetings per month for each City commission, unless
otherwise authorized by the City Council, in recognition of the limited staff
resources available to support the City’s commissions and the restoration of
one equity position dedicated to commission support; and to provide an
inventory of all City commissions, including the number of active ad hoc
committees associated with each commission and, where available, the staff
resources required to support those committees; and, based on this
information, return to the City Council with recommendations for reducing
both staff time and costs for commissions with the goal of ensuring equitable
use of staff resources across commissions and avoiding a disproportionate
allocation of staff capacity to a subset of commissions or committees.

[B26] Motion to recognize the recommendation of the Equity and Human
Relations Commission (EHRC) to establish a Civil and Human Rights
Investment Screening Policy, developed following community advocacy and
public input, and subsequently revised in response to concerns raised by the
Financial Management Department regarding fiscal impacts, feasibility, and
implementation; and, consistent with the City Manager’s recommendation
that further consideration occur through the FY 27 budget process, direct the
City Manager to work with the Financial Management Department to amend
the City Council’s Investment Policy to incorporate a civil and human rights
investment screening element, inclusive of the following modifications
discussed and agreed upon by the Budget Oversight Committee on August
28, 2026:

1. Evidence-Based Compliance Standard. Replace the proposed presumption
of noncompliance with an evidence-based compliance standard by revising
Section 2.5 to authorize the City’s Investment Manager to make a good-faith
determination of compliance based on credible, independently verifiable
information from reliable third-party sources specializing in civil and human
rights risk assessments and responsible investment screening.

2. Integration with Existing Investment Reporting. Remove the proposed
stand-alone annual reporting requirement and instead incorporate reporting
on implementation of the Policy into the City’s existing investment reporting
process to reduce administrative burden while maintaining transparency and
public accountability.

3. Immigration Detention and Border Surveillance. Expand the prohibited
investment criteria to include companies that own, operate, finance, or
materially support border surveillance or immigration detention facilities,
including companies that materially facilitate border surveillance or

  Page 7 of 11
   BUDGET OVERSIGHT COMMITTEE MINUTES
  TUESDAY, SEPTEMBER 8, 2026
  411 W. OCEAN BOULEVARD
  CIVIC CHAMBERS, 1:00 PM

immigration detention through government contracts, consistent with the
Policy’s broader civil and human rights framework.

The amended Investment Policy shall otherwise incorporate civil and human
rights investment screening criteria addressing entities shown to be complicit
in: (i) genocide, apartheid, occupation, displacement, or other human rights
violations; (ii) labor rights violations; (iii) state violence; (iv) environmental
harm; (v) inadequate supply chain due diligence; and/or (vi) inadequate
corporate governance standards. Direct the City Manager to return to the City
Council with the proposed amended Investment Policy for review and
approval, along with any funding request necessary to implement the Policy
through specialized screening software or an advisor-managed solution.

[B27] Motion to clarify language from FY 26 Adopted Budget BOC motion
(B44) to establish the second-to-last Budget Oversight Committee (BOC)
meeting as the deadline for City Council budget recommendations to be
heard and considered by the Committee, ensuring adequate time to develop
final recommendations for City Council.

As a result of a memo to the City Council on July 1, 2025, providing additional
guidance and transparency regarding engagement with the BOC, this motion
would require all City Council budget request memos to be submitted with
sufficient time for the recommendation to be agendized and heard no later
than the second-to-last BOC meeting. The final BOC meeting would not
include Council correspondence or consideration of new budget request
memos and would instead be reserved for finalizing the Committee’s
recommendations to City Council. Council correspondence received after the
submission deadline would be included in the legislative record under non-
agenda public comment; however, its inclusion would not provide an
opportunity for Committee discussion.

[B28] Motion to acknowledge that requests for funding from Council Districts
for various programs and services have been received and reviewed. At this
time, due to fiscal challenges limiting possible funding resources, these
requests cannot be recommended for incorporation into the proposed Fiscal
Year 2027 Budget. The programs and services listed below remain on file for
future consideration, pending availability of resources or alternative funding
mechanisms. This motion serves to recognize the value of these initiatives
while maintaining fiscal responsibility and transparency in the budgeting
process:

1. Restoration of Fire Engine 14
2. Restoration Police Patrol Staffing
3. Additional structural funding towards the Long Beach Justice Fund
4. Additional funding towards Youth Participatory Budgeting

6. Restoration of Code Enforcement Inspector
7. Fire Station 14 Fast Response Vehicle Pilot
8. Restoration of Homeless Employment/Workforce Development
9. Restoration of Weekend Homeless Outreach
10. Funding to The Nonprofit Partnership to continue its work supporting
nonprofit organizations and community-based partners in West Long Beach
through the Westside Promise. The motion carried by the following vote:

Yes:  2  Uranga, Ricks-Oddie
No:  1  Allen
